title: Oceans and Continents — Chapter Summary
intro: About 71% of the Earth is covered by water and 29% by land. The seven big landmasses are called CONTINENTS; the five big bodies of water are called OCEANS. This chapter introduces the continents in order of size, the five oceans and where each lies, and India's place in the world.

sections.heading: Land and Water
bullets: About 71% of Earth's surface is water; 29% is land.
Big bodies of water are called oceans; smaller bodies are seas, gulfs, bays, lakes, rivers.
Big landmasses are continents; smaller ones are islands.
All five oceans are connected — water flows freely. Together they form one 'world ocean'.
Continents are mostly separate landmasses (some are islands).

sections.heading: The Seven Continents
bullets: ASIA — largest, ~30% of all land. Home of the Himalayas, India, China, Japan.
AFRICA — second-largest. Sahara desert, Nile river, great wildlife.
NORTH AMERICA — third. Canada, USA, Mexico; Rocky Mountains.
SOUTH AMERICA — fourth. Amazon, Andes, Brazil.
ANTARCTICA — fifth. Coldest, ice-covered, no permanent residents.
EUROPE — sixth. Many small countries; the Alps; densely populated.
AUSTRALIA — smallest. Kangaroos, Great Barrier Reef. Sometimes called Oceania.

sections.heading: The Five Oceans
bullets: PACIFIC — largest and deepest. Between Asia/Australia and the Americas. Covers ~30% of Earth's surface.
ATLANTIC — second. Between Americas and Europe/Africa. 'S' shape.
INDIAN — third. South of Asia, west of Australia, east of Africa.
SOUTHERN (Antarctic) — fourth. Surrounds Antarctica.
ARCTIC — smallest. Surrounds the North Pole; mostly ice.

sections.heading: Major Features of Each Continent
bullets: Asia → Himalayas, Gobi desert, Ganga / Yangtze rivers.
Africa → Sahara desert, Nile river, savanna wildlife.
North America → Rockies, Mississippi, Great Lakes.
South America → Andes, Amazon rainforest, Atacama desert.
Antarctica → ice cap, South Pole.
Europe → Alps, Mediterranean coast, dense rail.
Australia → Great Barrier Reef, outback, unique animals.

sections.heading: India in the World
bullets: India is in the southern part of ASIA.
Indian Ocean to the south; Bay of Bengal to the east; Arabian Sea to the west.
Sri Lanka lies south of India across the Palk Strait.
Tropic of Cancer passes through India → most of India is in the Torrid Zone (hot).
Land neighbours: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh.
The Himalayas form a natural northern barrier.

key_takeaways: Seven continents (largest to smallest): Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.
Five oceans (largest to smallest): Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic.
Antarctica is the coldest; Pacific is the largest and deepest.
India is in Asia, on the Indian Ocean, with the Tropic of Cancer through the middle.
India's land neighbours: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh.

glossary.definition: A very large landmass on Earth — there are seven.
A very large body of salt water — there are five.
A smaller body of salt water, usually partly enclosed by land.
A part of the sea or ocean that extends into the land in a wide curve (e.g. Bay of Bengal).
The largest continent, including India and many other countries.
The second-largest continent, with the Sahara desert and the Nile river.
The coldest continent, almost entirely covered in ice; contains the South Pole.
The smallest continent; sometimes called Oceania when including surrounding islands.
The largest and deepest ocean, between Asia/Australia and the Americas.
The second-largest ocean, between the Americas and Europe/Africa.
The third-largest ocean, south of Asia, with India at its northern edge.
The ocean surrounding Antarctica; also called the Antarctic Ocean.
The smallest ocean, surrounding the North Pole; mostly ice-covered.
The large bay east of India, part of the Indian Ocean.
The sea west of India, part of the Indian Ocean.
